PHYSICS — TERMLY EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: PHYSICS
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

2. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. pascal (Pa)
   B. newton (N)
   C. joule (J)
   D. watt (W)

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Transistors? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Transistors.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Transistors.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Transistors.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Transistors.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Floating and Sinking? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Floating and Sinking.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Floating and Sinking.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Floating and Sinking.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Floating and Sinking.

5. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Producers
   B. Decomposers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Primary consumers only

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mains electricity? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mains electricity.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mains electricity.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mains electricity.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Mains electricity.

7. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Dynamics? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Dynamics.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dynamics.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Dynamics.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Dynamics.

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites.

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 37 °C
   D. 100 °C

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Photoelectric effect? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Photoelectric effect.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Photoelectric effect.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Photoelectric effect.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Photoelectric effect.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Circular motion? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Circular motion.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Circular motion.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Circular motion.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Circular motion.

13. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS.

15. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

16. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Removing all vegetation
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Thin lenses and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Photoelectric effect and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Electromagnetic induction and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Mains electricity and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Transistors and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Satellites Page 12 of 49 1 STRAND 1.0 MECHANICS AND THERMAL PHYS and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
